text:
sanjay: FYI seeing a cluster-wide perf regression for multi-GPU jobs in us-west-2 after last night's driver/kernel push. NCCL is falling back off NVLink to SHM/NET on mixed P2P topologies.
lin: Which nodes are hitting it? logs?
maya: A handful in prod-gpu-3 pool: gpu-3a-02, gpu-3a-05, gpu-3b-01. Jobs queueing, throughput down ~3x on resnet-bench.
rene: I grabbed a quick `nvidia-smi topo -m` from gpu-3a-02:
```
        Gpu0 Gpu1 CPU Affinity
Gpu0     X   NV1   0-11
Gpu1    NV1    X   0-11

Legend: NV# = NVLink#
```
But NVLink shows disconnected for some pairs on other nodes:
```
        Gpu0 Gpu1 Gpu2
Gpu0     X   P2P   X
Gpu1    P2P    X   X
Gpu2     X     X   X
```
lin: That second matrix looks like NVLink not being detected and NCCL using P2P via SHM/NET fallback. Any kernel logs?
sanjay: dmesg on gpu-3b-01 shows repeated: `nvidia: NVLINK: link 1 failed to initialize` and `nvidia: p2p: peer memory not available`
rene: Also saw this in journalctl: `kernel: nvidia 0000:65:00.0: failed to register nvlink topology - missing kernel symbol nvlink_get_link_state`
maya: We rolled driver 535.86 -> 536.33 during the window. Some nodes were also on a newer kernel patch (5.15.0-87 vs 5.15.0-86) due to livepatch stagger. Mixed kernel/driver combo maybe the root.
alex: That mismatch could cause kernel module ABI differences -> some nvlink symbols not exported to modules. Did the packaging pipeline rebuild kernel modules against the kernel?
lin: I checked kube images: nodes with repro had `nvidia.ko` version 536.33 but kernel module shows `tainted: incompatible-kernel` in dmesg on affected hosts.
ops-bot: Deployment note: driver rollout started 1778121200, node batch 3 hit between 1778123200-1778123300.
sanjay: Quick mitigation option: pin scheduler to avoid affected nodes (taint + cordon) and roll back driver on the small set. We don't want to evict long-running jobs unless necessary.
maya: Agreed. Also toggling `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on job envs will force socket paths but that loses perf. For immediate triage can set `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` to collect logs.
lin: Requested diagnostic commands for eng-sre to run:
```
# on host
modinfo nvidia | grep -E "version|srcversion"
nvidia-smi topo -m
journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver.service --since "-30m" | tail -n 200
lsmod | grep nvlink
cat /sys/kernel/debug/nvlink/* || true
```
rene: I posted outputs in the bug ticket. One interesting bit: `lsmod` shows nvlink module absent on two nodes but present on their siblings. Means module failed to load (missing symbols).
alex: Temporary workaround: force restart the nvidia-driver pod to pick up correct module loader ordering after kernel livepatch, but if symbols truly missing that's insufficient.
maya: We should open an NVIDIA support case with: driver version, kernel version, dmesg snippet, `modinfo`, and a small repro (topo + NCCL perf test). I'm drafting the ticket.
lin: For rollout plan: 1) cordon/taint affected nodes, 2) roll back to 535.x on the small set and verify NVLink detection, 3) repro NCCL perf, 4) if rollback fixes, schedule a staggered re-roll with kernel-module rebuild verification.
sanjay: Also add a preflight: after driver push, run `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` + `nvidia-smi topo -m` smoke check on a canary host before marking batch done.
ops-bot: Action items assigned: @maya open support case, @lin run diagnostics on 3a-05 and 3b-01, @rene collect dmesg + modinfo bundle, @sanjay coordinate cordon/rollbacks.
maya: I'll attach perf numbers: resnet throughput drop from 6200 images/s -> 2100 images/s when NVLink drops. That's consistent with NCCL choosing NET path.
alex: Longer term: add module export/version checks to driver roll pipeline and a kernel-driver compatibility matrix to avoid mixed state. Also consider auto-drain of nodes that lost nvlink after patching.
lin: If you need immediate list of affected instances I dumped labels/annotations: `nodepool=prod-gpu-3` + `driver_version=536.33` + `kernel_patch=5.15.0-87`. I'll share the CSV in the ticket.
rene: One more note: we saw one host where manual `modprobe nvlink` succeeded after unloading `nvidia_uvm` first, then `nvidia` module auto-loaded nvlink. That suggests load order matters.
sanjay: Good catch. Include that in the runbook. Next: execute cordon on the two worst nodes now and start rollbacks (non-urgent but needs <2h work).
maya: I'll update ticket and post back with NVIDIA response. :raising_hand:
lin: Thanks team. Keep the thread updated with rollback results.
